contract.proves:
NEGATIVE CONTROL for the harness restoration law.

This scenario deliberately leaves residue: it stops a node and never restores
it — there is no `start_node` in steps and no cleanup section at all. It is
the test that proves the detector can fire.

Expected behaviour of the RUNNER (not of the product):
  1. the mutation ledger records node_stopped(node-5);
  2. teardown finds it outstanding after cleanup;
  3. teardown reverses it (docker start) and verifies the container is running;
  4. the scenario is marked FAILED with "RESIDUE: scenario left unrestored
     mutations", even though every assertion in it passes.

A scenario whose assertions all pass but which leaks state MUST fail. If this
scenario ever reports PASS, the restoration law is not being enforced and
every other destructive scenario is free to contaminate its successors —
which is exactly what happened on 2026-08-05, when a detached etcd member and
a root-owned service key rode silently into three later suites.

This is intentionally the only scenario in the tree that is SUPPOSED to fail.
Do not "fix" it by adding cleanup — that would delete the control.
